description: Close the compounding gaps that let the container-mode sidecar die silently on firewall-init (dnsmasq port 53) failure: durable marker surfacing, a liveness watcher with bounded respawn, sidecarAlive gates, and port-53 root-cause teardown.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Confirmed `docker rm -f` stops (SIGKILL) and removes a running container in one call; this is the correct one-shot teardown for the stale cam-worker container at session exit (story 4). Docs do not specify exit behavior when the container is absent, so the teardown must tolerate a non-zero exit (best-effort, never throw).

userStories.title: Durable sidecar-stalled marker written on firewall-init failure and surfaced at orchestrator boot
userStories.description: As the operator, I need a firewall-init failure of the container sidecar to leave a durable marker that the orchestrator surfaces at boot, so a dead sidecar is visible instead of writing a plan/meta-loop signal into the void.
acceptanceCriteria: A new module src/supervisor/sidecar-stalled.ts exports SIDECAR_STALLED_FILENAME = '.cam-sidecar-stalled.json', a SidecarStalledMarker interface with a structured `reason` field (usable by both producers: 'firewall-init-failed' and, later, 'sidecar-died'), plus `detail` and `writtenAt`, and never-throwing read/write/remove helpers mirroring src/supervisor/plan-escalation.ts. [oracle: grep -q "SIDECAR_STALLED_FILENAME = '.cam-sidecar-stalled.json'" src/supervisor/sidecar-stalled.ts]

The read helper returns null on absent / malformed-JSON / wrong-shape input and never throws; write and remove never throw (JSON reader shape-guard pattern, validate the discriminator fields not just typeof). [oracle: bun test]

The FirewallError arm in src/commands/sidecar.ts (runContainerEnsureGuard, ~line 2754) writes the marker with reason 'firewall-init-failed' and the stderrTail as detail before returning abort=true. [oracle: bun test]

The marker is removed on the next healthy sidecar bring-up (mirroring the plan-escalated remove-on-converge lifecycle: removed in the boot path when the container ensure guard passes / in host mode where the guard is a no-op). [oracle: bun test]

templates/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md boot-read list and opening-blocker section surface the new marker with an opening blocker line ⚠ sidecar stalled: <reason> — <detail>, added alongside the existing ship-stalled / plan-escalated / plan-preflight-failed markers, and instruct the orchestrator not to delete it (read-only at boot). [oracle: grep -q 'sidecar stalled' templates/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md]
templates/.gitignore includes .cam-sidecar-stalled.json. [oracle: grep -q '.cam-sidecar-stalled.json' templates/.gitignore]
Vendor drift check passes (bun run embed-vendor:check) after regenerating the embedded copy with bun run embed-vendor. [oracle: bun run embed-vendor:check]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Lint spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: New file src/supervisor/sidecar-stalled.ts is a near-verbatim structural copy of src/supervisor/plan-escalation.ts (filename const + interface + read/write/remove, never-throw). The single shared marker file has two producers (this story: firewall arm; US-002: watcher) distinguished by the `reason` field — do NOT create two separate marker files (gotcha). Firewall arm is at src/commands/sidecar.ts runContainerEnsureGuard (~2746-2775, FirewallError branch ~2754); remove-on-healthy goes in the boot path of runSidecar (~2786+) after the ensure guard returns false. Container-gated producer is naturally host-inert (the firewall arm only runs in container mode); do not claim live validation.

userStories.title: Sidecar-liveness watcher with sidecarAlive() composite, bounded respawn, and escalate-on-exhaustion
userStories.description: As the operator, I need a background watcher that detects a dead container sidecar and either respawns it (bounded) or escalates via the shared marker, so a silently-dead sidecar is recovered or surfaced instead of leaving the session wedged.
acceptanceCriteria: A composite sidecarAlive(claudeDir) is added to src/supervisor/sidecar-pid.ts (mirroring watcherAlive at ~line 153): returns true iff .cam-sidecar.pid exists, parses to a positive integer, and signal-0 confirms the process is alive; false otherwise; never throws. [oracle: grep -q 'export function sidecarAlive' src/supervisor/sidecar-pid.ts]

A new internal subcommand src/commands/sidecar-liveness-watch.ts mirrors src/commands/orch-recycle-watch.ts (poll loop + injectable pid-resolve/kill/spawn/sleep/marker seams), discovers the sidecar via sidecarAlive(), and on a dead sidecar attempts a bounded respawn (N attempts with backoff). [oracle: bun test]

On respawn exhaustion the watcher writes the shared .cam-sidecar-stalled.json marker with reason 'sidecar-died' and stops respawning (escalate, never hot-loop — no respawn of a sidecar that keeps dying on a deterministic firewall failure). [oracle: bun test]
The new command does NOT register a --permission-mode flag. [oracle: bun test]

Watcher spawn wiring is added to src/commands/run.ts alongside the orch-recycle-watch spawn (a new detached-not-really background child + persisted pid via the sidecar-pid.ts pattern), and cleanup/kill is added to src/commands/stop.ts. [oracle: grep -q 'sidecar-liveness-watch' src/commands/run.ts]
The watcher spawn is a no-op when worker_isolation != 'container' (host mode); validated by tests, not a live run (gotcha: this repo is host mode). [oracle: bun test]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]

userStories.title: cam plan / next / ship refuse the signal-write when the sidecar is dead
userStories.description: As the operator, I need cam plan, cam next, and cam ship to check sidecar liveness and refuse with a clear error when the sidecar is dead, so a phase:planning / active:true / phase:shipping signal is never orphaned into a silent hang.
acceptanceCriteria: cam plan (src/commands/plan.ts) checks sidecarAlive(claudeDir) in its liveness preamble and, when the sidecar is dead, refuses with a clear error (non-zero exit) and does NOT write phase:planning to .claude/cam-loop.local.md. [oracle: bun test]
cam next (src/commands/next.ts) checks sidecarAlive() and, when dead, refuses without writing active:true. [oracle: bun test]
cam ship (src/commands/ship.ts) checks sidecarAlive() and, when dead, refuses without writing phase:shipping. [oracle: bun test]
The gate applies in BOTH host and container modes (the orphaned-signal hang is isolation-agnostic; this is the one story that is not container-gated). [oracle: bun test]
Each command exposes an injectable sidecarAlive seam so tests exercise the dead/alive branches without touching real pids. [oracle: bun test]

userStories.notes: Depends on US-002 (consumes sidecarAlive() from src/supervisor/sidecar-pid.ts). Gate insertion points: plan.ts runPlan liveness/mutex preamble (~240-253, before buildPlanningBody write at ~262-265); next.ts preamble before the active:true write (~334-370, after the mutex check ~313-321); ship.ts liveness preamble (~137-160+, before the phase:shipping write). The refusal must occur BEFORE the state-file write so no orphaned signal is left. This gate is host-relevant — keep it mode-agnostic (do not wrap in a container check). Fixes the silent-hang half of the issue (cam plan liveness gate today checks only the orchestrator pane, exits 0 into a hang).

userStories.title: Root-cause port-53 fail-safe: container teardown at session exit + init-firewall reap-and-retry
userStories.description: As the operator, I need the cam-worker container torn down at session exit and the firewall init to reap a stale dnsmasq holding port 53 before binding, so a leftover container from a prior session cannot hard-wedge the next session.
acceptanceCriteria: src/commands/stop.ts tears down the cam-worker container at session exit via docker rm -f (DEFAULT_CONTAINER_NAME), gated to container mode (no-op when worker_isolation != 'container'), through an injectable spawn seam, best-effort (a non-zero exit when the container is absent is tolerated, never throws). [oracle: bun test]

.devcontainer/init-firewall.sh, on a port-53 collision, reaps the dnsmasq process actually holding the port (not only the pid in /var/run/dnsmasq-cam.pid), retries the bind once, and fails closed (non-zero exit) if the port is still blocked. [oracle: grep -q 'port 53' .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh]

The init-firewall reap logic and fail-closed exit are present and readable (shell logic reviewed for correctness; validated by inspection + stop.ts tests, not a live container run per the gotcha). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
All of this story is a no-op / inert when worker_isolation != 'container' (this repo is host mode). [oracle: bun test]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Lint spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Independent of US-001/002/003 (this fix alone prevents THIS specific wedge; 1/2/3 are defense-in-depth). Root cause: stop.ts today cleans only tmux/markers, never the container (~465-472); ensure-container.ts reuses a running cam-worker (~335-337), inheriting its stale dnsmasq. Tearing the container down at exit means the next session restarts fast (or rebuilds only if image-stale) via the existing absent->build path. DEFAULT_CONTAINER_NAME ('cam-worker') is exported from ensure-container's constants (src/supervisor/ensure-container.ts imports DEFAULT_CONTAINER_NAME ~line 25). init-firewall.sh port-53 block is at .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh ~34-72 (today only kills the pid in /var/run/dnsmasq-cam.pid, ~43-46; extend to detect+reap the actual port holder + one retry + fail-closed). init-firewall.sh is NOT embedded/vendored (no embed-vendor:check needed for this story). docker rm -f confirmed to SIGKILL+remove a running container in one call. Gate stop.ts teardown via readWorkerIsolation (src/config/models.ts:300-315, fail-closes to host).
